definitions.explanation: The larger form of a letter in alphabets that distinguish between two cases, such as A, B, C in the Latin alphabet. Contrasted with {小文字|こもじ} (lowercase).

examples.japanese: {大文字|おおもじ}で{書|か}いてください。
パスワードには{大文字|おおもじ}と{小文字|こもじ}を{混|ま}ぜてください。
examples.english: Please mix uppercase and lowercase letters in your password.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}では{文|ぶん}の{最初|さいしょ}の{文字|もじ}を{大文字|おおもじ}にするのがルールだ。
examples.english: In English, the rule is to capitalize the first letter of a sentence.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {大|おお} (large) + {文字|もじ} (character, letter). Primarily used when discussing the Latin alphabet or other writing systems with case distinctions.

NOTE:
The reading おおもじ means uppercase letter. The same kanji can also be read だいもんじ, which refers to the famous Daimonji bonfire on a mountainside in Kyoto during the Obon festival.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大文字|おおもじ}と{小文字|こもじ} (uppercase and lowercase)
- {大文字|おおもじ}に{変換|へんかん}する (to convert to uppercase)
- {大文字|おおもじ}{小文字|こもじ}を{区別|くべつ}する (to distinguish between upper and lower case)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {小文字|こもじ}: lowercase letter — the smaller form of a letter
